Open Source Intel ISRAEL ELECTIONS: Where do we stand? Gadi Eisenkot has until December 6 to form Israel’s next government, with a possible 14 day extension. Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister. Eisenkot’s bloc won 48 seats, Netanyahu’s bloc won 53, and the Arab parties won 19. A majority in the Knesset is 61. Eisenkot’s bloc has just 1 coalition deal so far, between his Yashar party and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu. Channel 12 reports that Lieberman is expected to return as defense minister and his party is also expected to get immigration. Naftali Bennett is being considered for finance, and Yair Lapid could return as foreign minister. The cabinet lineup is still under negotiation. Eisenkot is also negotiating with Likud over a possible unity government. The 2 sides still disagree over who would serve as prime minister first. Those talks prompted Yair Golan’s Democrats to freeze their negotiations with Yashar. The Democrats also oppose national security as ISRAEL ELECTIONS: Where do we stand? Gadi Eisenkot has secured his first coalition deal and is aiming to have a government sworn in as early as December 2, Channel 12 reports. He has yet to show he can win the Knesset vote. His mandate runs through December 6, with a possible 14 day extension. Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister. So far, only Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu has reached a deal with Eisenkot’s Yashar party. Channel 12 reports that Lieberman is expected to return as defense minister, with his party also taking responsibility for immigration. Naftali Bennett is being considered for finance, and Yair Lapid could return as foreign minister. Eisenkot is also discussing a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud. They still disagree over who would serve as prime minister first. Those talks prompted Yair Golan’s Democrats to freeze their own negotiations with Eisenkot. The Democrats also oppose taking national security as their most senior post. They want defense, foreign affairs or finance, or both education and justice. The optimism about December 2 comes partly from talks with United Torah Judaism over military draft exemptions for yeshiva students. Lieberman expects the party to back Eisenkot. Even if all 7 of its lawmakers do, and Eisenkot holds his entire bloc of 48 together, including the Democrats, that gives him 55 of 120 seats. Shas has the 6 seats needed to reach 61, but says it backs Netanyahu. Mansour Abbas’s Arab Ra’am party could bring Eisenkot to 63 if all 8 of its lawmakers vote for him. He could also win with 55 votes to 54 if 11 lawmakers abstain or stay away. Both scenarios run into the same problem if they depend on Arab parties. Lieberman says he would vote against such a government, and his 7 lawmakers are already counted in the 55. That is the question still hanging over December 2: who gives Eisenkot the votes to take office? tweet

Open Source Intel NEW: Netanyahu Trial Judges Call In Attorney General, Urge Her to Drop Bribery Charge Jerusalem District Court judges called Attorney General Gali Baharav Miara to court on November 25 and urged her to reassess the charges after Netanyahu finished testifying. In Case 4000, the judges questioned whether prosecutors could prove bribery or breach of trust and suggested dropping the bribery charge. In Case 2000, they questioned whether the conduct described in the indictment amounts to a crime. In Case 1000, the gifts case, they said most of the evidence had been heard and urged both sides to work toward a plea deal or a verdict. Baharav Miara said prosecutors would review the judges’ concerns and remain open to a plea deal. - N12 tweet

🔊 Iran seeks peace but will not yield to pressure: Ambassador 📌 London, IRNA – Iran’s new ambassador to Italy says Tehran is ready to resolve its disputes and tensions with Washington through diplomacy, but it will never surrender to pressure. In an interview with Corriere della Sera, Ali Akbar Rezaei said the negotiation process has not stopped, though it is progressing slowly. “We say ‘no’ to nuclear weapons and to surrender, while at the same time we support diplomacy and respect for international law.” ​ “If the other side is truly interested in ending the war, we are ready to take steps in that direction,” He added. ​ The ambassador called for Europe to play an independent role in international developments, saying that if the EU's 27 member states had reacted jointly and courageously, Donald Trump would not have been able to withdraw from the JCPOA so easily in 2018, and there probably would be no war today. ​ Regarding developments in the Strait of Hormuz, the diplomat stated: “Due to the attacks carried out against Iran, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz can no longer change into its previous state.” ​ “Nuclear weapons have no place in Iran’s nuclear doctrine. Our current weapons possess a very good deterrent power, and we intend to use nuclear energy solely for peaceful activities,” Rezaei added. 📲 @Irna_en ​

🇺🇸 ⚡️ The USAID Files, released on USAID.gov this morning, reveal communications between USAID staff and social media companies like Google and Meta, as well as “disinformation guidebooks.” A 2022 seminar featured Danny Rogers, co-founder of the Global Disinformation Index (GDI), who suggested USAID defund, downrank, and deplatform unwanted speech, describing disinformation as neither true nor false. Rogers cited Breitbart News as an example and outlined a framework for identifying “adversarial narratives.” USAID invited all employees to a 1-hour presentation by GDI’s executive director to develop social media censorship programs. GDI reportedly placed nearly every major conservative news outlet in America on an ad blacklist, resulting in a $200 million loss in ad revenue, a move recommended by the US intelligence community. The files also indicate that fact-checkers are intended to “debunk information in a way that aligns with the objectives of government partners.”
